{{Short description|American baseball statistician}}
'''Charles''' "'''Chuck'''" '''Waseleski''' (November 30, 1954 – April 7, 2016)<ref name=Legacy/> was an American pioneering [[sabermetrician]] from Massachusetts.

Waseleski was called "the czar of hardball software" by ''[[Boston Globe]]'' sportswriter [[Dan Shaughnessy]],<ref name=RedSoxNation/> but was most famously known in Boston as "The Maniacal One", a sobriquet often seen on the sports pages of the ''Globe''. The nickname, coined by [[Steve Fainaru]] and continued in use by [[Gordon Edes]], [[Peter Gammons]], and [[Nick Cafardo]], honored Waseleski's extreme attention to detail.<ref name=Farewell/><ref name=RedSoxNation/>

Waseleski, more a statistics compiler than an analyst, kept track for many years of every pitch and every ball in play of every [[Boston Red Sox]] game,<ref name=RedSoxNation/> during the early days of sabermetrics when this data was not routinely compiled.<ref name=Farewell/>

Waseleski did not practice sabermetrics as a full-time profession (he worked for an engineering consulting firm), although he did publish monthly and seasonal reports for a while and was employed by [[sports agent]]s,<ref name=RedSoxNation/><ref name=Farewell/> and excerpts of his work appeared in works by [[Bill James]]<ref name=BillJames/> and in ''Globe'' [[newspaper column]]s<ref name=Farewell/> beginning in the 1980s.<ref name=SonsOfSamHorn/>
